pipeline_name: El Tina- Abu Sultan- New Administrative Capital Gas Pipeline

resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' confirmed. Town Gas (EGAS distribution co) states the line 'تم تشغيله في يوليه 2019' (put into service July 2019); the Petroleum Ministry national-grid PDF lists 'خط غاز التينة/ابو سلطان/العاصمة الادارية (المرحلة الاولى والثانية)' among lines EXECUTED during 2014/15–Dec 2020 (i.e. completed/in service). egy-map.com project page also marks it completed. Status inferred from in-service/inauguration prose per confidence_tiers. url_verifier passed the ministry PDF (200 + '165' present); the Town Gas live host times out so the Wayback snapshot is cited and was confirmed to contain the entry (yields 'يوليه 2019').

Fuel 'Gas' confirmed. Ministry PDF names it 'خط غاز ... الغاز الطبيعي' (natural gas line). The independent EIB environmental-impact document is titled 'GASCO El Tina – Abu Sultan Onshore Gas Pipeline' and describes it feeding power stations 'by natural gas'. Both verified live (200); ministry PDF passed the substring screen, EIB PDF text confirmed via pdftotext.

StartYear1=2019 confirmed. Town Gas and egy-map.com both give exact date 'يوليه/يوليو 2019' (July 2019); ministry PDF places it among 2014/15–Dec-2020 executed lines (consistent). Marked medium/not-independent because the two date-bearing Arabic sources are official-family texts with near-verbatim wording, so likely trace to one ministry release; the EIB doc is an EIA (pre-construction) and carries no operation date. GEM stores only the year (2019); the underlying month is July.

LengthKnown=165 km confirmed. Ministry PDF: 'بطول 165 كم'; egy-map.com project page: '165 كم'; Town Gas: 'بطول 165 كم'. The EIB EIA / Petrojet contractor listing independently frame the line as '42"-165 KM', corroborating the figure across a genuinely separate (technical/contractor) origin. Ministry PDF passed url_verifier with '165'; egy-map is JS-rendered (verifier saw 200 but not the token) and the value was confirmed by fetching the rendered page.

Diameter=42 in confirmed. Ministry PDF: 'وقطر 42 بوصة'; egy-map.com: '42 بوصة'; Town Gas: 'وقطر 42 بوصة'. Independently corroborated by the Petrojet contractor project title 'El Tina-new capital (42"-165 KM)'. Ministry PDF passed url_verifier; egy-map value confirmed via rendered fetch (page is JS-rendered).

Route El Tina/Abu Sultan → New Administrative Capital confirmed. Ministry PDF and Town Gas name the line 'التينة/ابو سلطان/العاصمة الادارية'. egy-map.com lists the governorates traversed as Cairo, Ismailia and Port Said — consistent with StartState/Province=Port Said (El Tina/Abu Sultan is in the Port Said/Ismailia canal zone) and EndState/Province=Cairo (New Administrative Capital, east of Cairo). The independent EIB EIA details the El Tina–Abu Sultan onshore alignment (Bilbeis–Sarabium road, tie-in north of Abu Sultan). Note: egy-map adds Ismailia governorate along the corridor, which the GEM row does not capture as a waypoint — not a conflict, just finer granularity.

SegmentCost=3,335,000,000 EGP confirmed exactly. Town Gas: 'التكلفة الاستثمارية للمشروع حوالي 3335 مليون جنيه'; egy-map.com: '3 مليار و335 مليون جنيه' (= 3.335 bn EGP). Marked medium/not-independent: the two cost-bearing sources are official-family Arabic texts with near-verbatim wording (likely one ministry origin); the ministry national-grid PDF gives only an aggregate program cost, not this per-line figure, and the EIB doc has no cost. Wayback snapshot cited for Town Gas (live host times out) and confirmed to contain the value; egy-map confirmed via rendered fetch.

Owner value is 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS), 100%. The independent EIB environmental-impact document for this line names the developer/operator as 'Egyptian Natural Gas Co. (GASCO)' — GASCO is EGAS's national gas-transmission subsidiary, which owns and operates the national grid this line belongs to. CONTRADICTION/NUANCE TO FLAG: the source attributes the line to GASCO (the operating subsidiary), whereas the GEM Owner is set to the parent holding company EGAS. Both are correct at different corporate levels (GASCO ⊂ EGAS); consider whether GASCO should be the recorded owner/operator, or EGAS retained as ultimate owner. No source found stating a 100% EGAS equity split explicitly. EIB PDF verified live (200); 'GASCO'/'Egyptian Natural Gas Co.' confirmed via pdftotext.
